messages.content: Write the introduction to a monthly engineering newsletter whose theme this month is technical debt. Around 200 words.

Somewhere in this codebase is a file people quietly route around. We have more than one.

We treat technical debt like traffic: everyone complains, nobody owns it. That's a comfortable story, and it's false. Debt is what our own choices left behind, most of them defensible, made against deadlines that were real at the time. The auth shim shipped because the alternative was a missed launch. It worked. It's still running four years later, and three services now depend on the exact shape of its mistakes.

The debt doesn't grow. The interest does. A shortcut that cost one engineer an afternoon in 2022 costs the on-call rotation a bad night in 2026, and whoever pays that bill rarely signed for it.

Inside: [NAME] on the payments migration and why the second attempt held; [NAME] on scrapping our debt backlog in favor of budgeted hours; and a dissent arguing that some of our debt should be declared bankrupt and left exactly where it sits.

One request. When something ugly costs you time this month, write down the minutes, not the adjectives. We can argue about priorities forever. We can't argue with a number.

*(~200 words. Replace the auth shim and payments migration with your own examples — the specifics are what keep this from reading as filler.)*
Rewrite the text above. Keep the same length and the same purpose. Return only the rewritten text.

output:
There's a module in this repo nobody edits without first checking who else is awake. There are several.

We talk about technical debt the way we talk about weather: constant complaint, no author. Tidy story, and untrue. Every shortcut has a name on it, and most of those names made a defensible call against a deadline that was real. The auth shim shipped because the alternative was slipping the launch. It did the job. Four years later it's still in the request path, and three services depend on the precise shape of its compromises.

The principal stays flat. The interest compounds. An afternoon saved in 2022 becomes a 3am page in 2026, and whoever holds the pager never signed the loan.

This issue: [NAME] on the payments migration and why the second attempt stuck; [NAME] on killing our debt backlog in favor of budgeted hours; and a dissent arguing that some of our debt is worth writing off and leaving exactly where it lies.

One ask. When something ugly eats your time this month, log the minutes, not the adjectives. Priorities we can argue about indefinitely. A number is harder to wave away.

*(~200 words. Swap the auth shim and payments migration for your own — the specifics are what stop this reading as filler.)*
